Subject: Post-call: RTBF / data deletion workflow & next steps

Thanks again for the call today great to meet the FintechCo team. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the Right to Be Forgotten / data deletion items we discussed: 

Summary of FintechCo asks (as we understand them):
- PII deletion on user request (RTBF) with proof of deletion for compliance audits.
- Active data purge target: 30 days from request.
- Backups: must be removed / made unrecoverable within 90 days where feasible; ask for any immutable snapshot constraints.
- Data residency: US-only processing and storage for the tenant.
- Audit logs / deletion attestations for regulatory reviews (exportable CSV or signed statement).

What Redwood can do / next steps:
- Share our RTBF delete workflow doc and a short overview PDF (attached).
- Confirm specific SLA targets we can commit to for active purges and backup workflows after engineering review.
- Set up a 30-45 minute technical review with our infra team to walk the runbook and any proof artifacts (logs, checksums, deletion tickets).

Please confirm if the summary looks right and whether Legal should be looped in now (or after our technical session). Proposed times for the technical review: Thurs 3/26 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 3/27 09:00-10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila that summary is accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Active purge: 30 days is our target for removing PII from production indexes and primary storage. We understand caches/replicas should be flushed as part of that.
2) Backups: Our security team requires that backups containing PII be made unrecoverable within 90 days of a deletion request. We know some backup systems create immutable snapshots; if so, we need a documented mitigation approach (e.g., crypto-erase keys, legal attestations, or alternate retention settings).
3) Logs & audit: We need an exportable proof of deletion (deleted record IDs, timestamps, and the mechanism used) and access to audit logs showing the deletion workflow executed. Redaction or pseudonymization guidance for onboarding non-essential PII would also be helpful.

Looping in Legal for contract language around deletion SLAs and attestations.

Can we meet Thurs 3/26 at 10:00 PT - that works for our infra/security folks.

Alex
Director of Security & Compliance
FintechCo

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / data deletion workflow & next steps

Alex thanks, and noted. Quick technical outline ahead of tomorrow's session so the infra team can review in advance: 

High-level Redwood RTBF / deletion workflow (summary):
- Request intake: deletion ticket created (ID + requester metadata).
- Immediate actions: mark records as deleted (soft-delete flag) and remove from active indexes/serving caches (KV caches and in-memory models).
- Background purge: background job enqueues full object purge from object storage and DB; scope includes primary storage, secondary replicas, and search indexes.
- Backups & snapshots: we maintain snapshot retention policies; immutable snapshots are tracked. For customers requiring accelerated removal we have options: key-revocation/crypto-erase for encrypted snapshots, targeted snapshot pruning where provider allows, and documented attestation for immutable-provider constraints. Our default target for full unrecoverability is 90 days, but we can explore contract language for accelerated timelines where feasible.
- Audit evidence: upon completion we can export a signed deletion report (record ids + timestamps + job run ids) and provide the relevant audit log slices.

Known constraints and open items for the tech call:
- Cloud snapshot immutability windows (varies by provider); need to confirm FintechCo's cloud snapshot policies.
- Backup vendor SLA around forced deletions (some managed snapshot vendors don't allow immediate deletion).
- Legal/contractual attestations (we'll prepare a template).

Attached is a short runbook for the deletion workflow (rtbf-delete-workflow.md). During tomorrow's call we can walk the steps and identify any gaps.

Camila
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rtbf-delete-workflow.md (stub)
